subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call SLO follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call SLO follow-up

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap from the discovery and the next steps so we stay aligned before the validation run: 

Summary of SLOs you mentioned:
- Latency: p95 end-to-end <= 250 ms for non-streaming responses (typical request size ~600 tokens).
- Streaming: initial chunk latency <= 100 ms, smooth chunk rate thereafter.
- Throughput: sustained aggregate throughput target ~4k tokens/sec for 1k concurrent users (approx. 120 QPS, avg 600 tokens/request).
- Concurrency: burst concurrency up to ~60 simultaneous requests.

Validation objectives:
1) Verify Dedicated capacity sizing that meets the above SLOs for a production-like workload.
2) Compare GPU types (H100 vs A100) for latency/cost tradeoffs and recommend reserved throughput and GPU counts.
3) Confirm streaming behavior (gRPC streaming vs chunked HTTP) and end-to-end latency.

What we need from you before we schedule the run:
- Final SLO numbers you want us to validate and a sample workload (token distribution, typical prompt types).
- Any regional constraints (we can run in us-west-2 or us-east-1).
- Confirm whether you want H100 as the primary comparison or include L40/A2 as well for cost sensitivity.

Next steps we propose:
- You share the SLO doc/requirements (attach if handy).
- We provision a 2-hour validation window on Dedicated capacity, run against your sample workload, and deliver a perf report with recommended reserved throughput and expected costs.
- Post-run: concrete sizing recommendation (GPU counts + reserved throughput) and follow-on plan for rollout.

See a draft perf plan here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PerfTestPlan (we'll update the test matrix once you share the sample workload).

If that looks right, can we book the validation slot for Tue Nov 24 or Wed Nov 25?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa — this is exactly what we need. Attaching our SLO/requirements doc for the validation. Quick clarifications and priorities from our side:

Confirmed SLOs (final):
- Non-streaming p95 <= 220 ms (payloads ~400-800 tokens, median 600).
- Streaming: first-chunk <= 90 ms, subsequent chunk latency <= 70 ms.
- Sustained throughput target: 5k tokens/sec for our peak window.
- Concurrency: sustain up to 60 concurrent requests, with burst tolerance up to 120 for 30s.

Model note: we'll validate on the open 13B model variant we use (LM-13B-rlhf) — please assume the weights are similar to the Llama2 13B family for perf profiling.

GPU preference: we'd like H100 as the baseline. Please include A100 for a cost/latency comparison; if you can also show an L40 cost reference that would be helpful.

Region: us-west-2 preferred.

Attached: acme_slo_requirements.pdf

We'll be available Tue Nov 24 (afternoon PT) for the 2-hour slot. Please send a calendar invite with specifics.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Senior Platform Engineer, Acme Corp

Perfect — thanks for the SLO doc, Alex. I've penciled in Tue Nov 24 at 13:00 PT for a 2-hour validation window in us-west-2 and will send a calendar invite once Rafael confirms capacity.

High-level plan (what we will run during the 2-hour window):
- Smoke checks: model load, KV cache warmup, and single-request latency baseline (15 mins).
- H100 baseline: run incremental load tests to measure p50/p95/p99 latency across concurrency targets (45 mins).
- A100 comparison: same test matrix (30 mins).
- Streaming validation (gRPC streaming + HTTP chunking): measure first-chunk and steady-state chunk latency (20 mins).
- Post-run analysis and quick recommendations (10 mins).

Pre-validation asks from Acme:
- Upload a representative prompt set (10-50 prompts) to the shared Drive folder or confirm we'll use the sample set in the SLO doc.
- Confirm whether the model checkpoint will be provided or you want us to run on the Redwood-curated LM-13B equivalent.
- Point of contact during the run (we'll want an engineer to be available to triage).

I'll follow up with a calendar invite and the perf test matrix link. After the run we'll deliver a short report with recommended reserved throughput (tokens/sec), GPU count recommendations, and an estimated monthly cost for Dedicated capacity.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call SLO follow-up

Looping in a few technical notes before the run so we can optimize the validation time:

Quick recommendations based on Acme's targets:
- GPU comparisons: H100 will give the best latency headroom; A100 often hits reasonable latency at higher cost-per-token. L40 can be used as a cost-saver but may require more GPUs to meet the p95 target.
- Reserved throughput sizing (rough starting estimates, subject to validation):
  - H100 baseline: H100 x4 reserved with autoscaling/burst to x8 should meet p95 ~180-200 ms at concurrency 50 for LM-13B equiv.
  - A100 baseline: A100 x6 reserved (burst to x10) expected p95 ~210-260 ms under the same load.
  - L40 reference: L40 x8+ likely needed to hit similar throughput; we'll confirm in the test.
- Streaming: prefer gRPC streaming for lower first-byte latency; HTTP chunking is workable but increases variability depending on client/network stack. We'll test both.
- Warmup: KV cache warmup is important — plan a 5-10 minute warmup with representative prompts before measurement.
- Batching/quantization: we'll try moderate batch sizes and run both FP16 and 4-bit quantized paths (if model supports) to show cost/latency tradeoffs.

Please upload the prompt set to the Drive link Marissa shared and confirm whether you will provide a checkpoint. Also let us know if you want the perf report to include estimated monthly Dedicated commit pricing.

I'll bring the test harness and the perf dashboards so we can iterate in real time during the window.

– Aditya Rao
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
